newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian party says received cash from Dassault.
newsitem.headline: Belgian party says received cash from Dassault.

text.p: Belgium's Flemish Christian Democratic Party (CVP), now led by Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, on Tuesday confirmed a report it was given 1.2 million francs ($40,000) by French aerospace firm Dassault in 1987.
"Until 1989, under the law on party financing, gifts were perfectly legal," CVP spokesman Willy Buijs told Belga news agency.

The daily De Morgen newspaper said the independent Oversight Committee had given the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, a report saying the money was passed over in December 1987 when Wilfried Martens headed the then Christian Democrat-Liberal coalition.
It is not the first time Dassault's name has been connected with money allegedly paid to Belgian political parties, but it is the first time it has been connected with the CVP.

NATO Secretary General Willy Claes, a government economics minister for the Socialist Party in the late 1980s, was forced to resign in October last year over bribes alleged to have been paid to his party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta in exchange for for contracts.
Another Socialist minister at the time, Guy Coeme, was also forced to quit two and a half years ago for the same reasons.
A series of Christian Democrat-Socialist governments have held power since early 1988.
In May this year Belgium issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, head of Dassault Aviation, on suspicion of corruption.
He has denied allegations he paid 10 million French francs ($2 million) in bribes for a deal to modernise Belgian air force F16 and Mirage fighter jets.
